guide: Start with the business need
On Mandate, replace the fictional gap, outcome, perimeter and exclusions. Define why a capability is needed before choosing Buy.
Compare four routes
On Routes, compare Build, Buy, Partner and Do nothing. Include execution dependencies and the cost of delay or inaction. Cost/time limits are screens, not an automatic winner.
Cash funding basis

USD millions of incremental cash required from buyer plus financing over the common funding horizon in Mandate D32. Include cash consideration, debt repayment, fees, integration and incremental operating investment. Exclude noncash stock / rollover and undrawn facilities. The envelope is a screening limit, not proof of financing.
Timing basis
Months run from the fixed review date to usable capability. Do nothing has zero months to the decision to defer; it does not close the capability gap.
Mandate approval and revision

After any material mandate change, increment D27, reassess targets and renew approval. Enter the approved revision in D31. Approval recorded requires matching revisions, sponsor, authority, record and valid date. Arbitrary edits do not automatically increment the revision; the user must do this.
Criteria and reviewed basis

Six editable criteria have stable IDs, required flags and evidence tests. At least one must be required. Screen compares the reviewed basis in P with current basis Q; changed required criteria reopen. After reassessment copy Q to P as values and record the current revision in O.
Target records

Use 12 target slots T01–T12. Replace fictional names and facts. Keep IDs unique and stable across Targets and Screen. Record the reviewed mandate revision in Targets AH after reassessing target-level evidence. If you rename an ID, update every linked screen row.
User priority

Enter a unique positive whole number per active target. Lower means earlier review. Priorities do not need to be consecutive. Duplicate, blank, zero, negative or fractional priorities are excluded from the ranked queue and counted as unranked.
Evidence before eligibility

Screen holds one row per target and criterion. Meets requires Verified evidence, a source/reference, a dated finding and a current evidence date. Assumption, Unverified, Conflicting, Unknown and missing evidence remain Open.
Evidence age
A date after the review date is invalid. Evidence age equal to the entered maximum is allowed; older evidence is stale. Refresh the review date and evidence deliberately. No TODAY() formulas.
A negative finding
A required Fails finding holds the target even when the underlying claim is unverified. Confirm or refute it before advancement; the label does not establish that the claim is fact.
Optional criteria
A criterion marked No remains in the evidence register as Optional finding. It is excluded from required gate counts. Its risks still need human review.
Seller willingness
Open means evidence of a willingness to consider a transaction, not a commitment to sell. Not now holds the screen. Unknown remains Investigate.
Seller control

Identify who can deliver the required vote and assets. Missing control is an early hold. Unknown control requires investigation. The evidence reference on Targets should support the capital/time, willingness, control and veto assessments.
Consent-path exception

Missing control can become Conditional consent review only with a scarce or strategically imperative basis, a credible consent path, a documented exception approval and verified current evidence. It stays outside the eligible shortlist until control is confirmed.
Fatal veto and judgment

A Yes veto or Walk judgment always returns Walk, regardless of priority or other findings. Record an explicit pass rationale. Investigate, Price and Protect identify how to handle risk; they cannot override a failed hard gate.
Screen eligibility

Meets screen requires valid record and priority, defined mandate, capital/time within limits, no recorded required failure or unresolved required pair, verified target evidence, seller Open, no veto, stated confirmed control, and owner/action/due date.
Rank is not approval

The review queue includes held and Walk targets so the reasons remain visible. The separate eligible shortlist includes only Meets screen. Both follow your priority, not a weighted score. Mandate approval is shown separately.
Accountability

Enter a named owner, a next action and a real due date for each target before shortlist eligibility. An overdue date remains visible on Targets. Completion and outreach are not recorded by this workbook.
Sort and edit safely

Use the full Targets or Screen table filter/sort. Keep complete rows together. Evidence joins use IDs, so notes stay with their target. Do not sort a single column, overwrite formula columns or add rows beyond the 12-target / 72-screen capacity without extending and checking formulas.
Adding a target

Fill an unused target slot, assign a unique priority and complete its six Screen rows, including reviewed revision and basis. The dashboard updates automatically. A missing required pair stays open; duplicate pairs are invalid.
Assumption examples

All names, numbers, dates, motives and findings in the sample are fictional Assumption examples. They are not a transaction recommendation or claims about real businesses. Delete or replace them before real use.
What this does not assess

No valuation, financing commitment, debt-service coverage, tax/legal conclusion, formal diligence clearance or transaction approval is produced. Obtain the required advice and approvals for an actual process.
Acquisition Lens handoff
Use this workbook to define the mandate and shortlist. Use Acquisition Lens to examine an individual opportunity, then diligence, valuation, synergy and LOI tools as the decision develops.
